summary: A chaotic real-time game where you first scramble to slap together a spaceship from randomly drawn tiles under a running timer, then fly it through a gauntlet of meteors, pirates, and disasters hoping the shoddy build holds together. It's equal parts building-phase panic and flight-phase schadenfreude as ships lose engines, cargo, and crew piece by piece.
praised: huge replayability from random tiles and event decks
tension between greedy building and safe building
great for groups who enjoy laughing at their own disasters
criticised: heavy luck in what tiles you draw and what events hit
real-time segment stresses out some players
a ship can be crippled early with little to be done about it
less satisfying for players who want tight strategic control

interaction.kind: real-time competition for a shared tile pool, then relative-position collisions and attacks during flight
interaction.detail: The building phase has all players simultaneously grabbing from the same open pile of ship parts, so speed and snatching the piece a rival needs is core to the game. During flight, ships share the same route and relative movement means faster ships strike slower ones first, cannons and comets can wreck a rival's cargo or crew directly, turning the outcome into a running collision between everyone's ships rather than parallel play.
interaction.said: "chaotic", "real-time scramble", "everyone grabs for the same pile of tiles", "you will ram your friends' ships"

subsystems: build-and-fly integrated ship engine (building feeds directly into the flight survival phase)
sources: cargo sold at end of each flight
penalties for lost/destroyed components and crew
scoring.how_you_win: Build the best ship you can under time pressure, then survive three increasingly dangerous flights; the player with the most credits from cargo sales and encounters, minus losses, wins.

theme.said: 'frantic tile-slapping IS the theme,' 'you're basically building IKEA furniture at gunpoint,' rarely called abstract
theme.why: the real-time scramble to slap together a ship before the timer runs out models a rushed, cut-rate trucking outfit, and the ensuing flight where exposed crew and cargo get ripped off by meteors is a direct consequence of how sloppily you built in that scramble

style.why: A real-time build phase gives way to dice-driven hazards that can wreck ships and crew, with humor and survival mattering more than optimization even though there's no player-vs-player elimination
